correctness.rationale: For a=rζ the rational function h_a=b_a−a belongs to VMOA_0, and harmonic reproduction and unit boundary modulus give Φ_h(z)=1−|b_a(z)|². Its maximum is one at z=a. A common Lebesgue point of f and |f|² makes Φ_f vanish nontangentially. After rotating ζ to 1, write z=(r−w)/(1−rw) with |w|<=s<1. Then |1−z|=(1−r)|1+w|/|1−rw| and 1−|z|²=(1−r²)(1−|w|²)/|1−rw|². Their quotient bounds |1−z|/(1−|z|) by a constant depending only on s, while |1−z|=O_s(1−r), so the entire large-variance disk is in a fixed cone and Φ_f is uniformly small there. Minkowski bounds the mixed norm by |t|+o(1) inside the disk and by ||f||_G+|t|sqrt(1−s²) outside; take r→1 before s→1. For the matching lower bounds, at each fixed interior z the perturbation variance tends to zero and one may then take the supremum of the remaining Φ_f; at the moving z=a the perturbation has variance one and Φ_f(a)→0. This proves the law without assuming norm attainment. For every point of each closed ball, t=±1 gives a unit perturbation with both endpoint norms tending to one. The covariance spot check in RESULT.md follows by summing the geometric series for h_r(z)=−(1−r²)z/(1−rz); it is not the proof. Replay is symbolic via RESULT.md Steps 1–5; no code or mesh data is required.
